subject: math-ai-hl
title: Inflating a spherical balloon
subtopic: Related rates for volume and area
stem: A spherical balloon has volume $V=4\pi r^3/3$ and area $A=4\pi r^2$. Air enters at 2 cubic centimetres per second. Consider the instant when $r=3$ cm. Unless otherwise stated, give numerical answers exactly or to three significant figures.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the rate of increase of surface area.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain how the radius growth rate changes as the balloon enlarges at the same volume inflow.

steps.text: Differentiate volume with respect to time: $dV/dt=4\pi r^2\,dr/dt$.
Substitute the given volume rate and radius.
The radius rate is inversely proportional to $r^2$.
It decreases as the balloon grows.
The assumption of constant inflow must remain valid.
